entries.definition: characterized by physical misery
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gathers the discomfort into a whole bodily condition instead of a single sensation, so it reads as total rather than local.

entries.definition: causing physical discomfort
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heavier word for that same effect, putting the discomfort on the scale of hurt rather than annoyance.
examples: bites of black flies are more than irritating: they can be very painful

entries.definition: feeling physical discomfort or pain (‘tough’ is occasionally used colloquially for ‘bad’)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The colloquial counterpart to *bad*, looser and more offhand about the same felt discomfort.
examples: he was feeling tough after a restless night

entries.definition: providing or experiencing physical discomfort
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain cover term, working equally for the thing that gives the discomfort and the body that feels it, which is what keeps it so flat.
examples: an uncomfortable day in the hot sun

entries.definition: relating to bodily unease that causes discomfort
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The faintest of these: a bodily unsettledness that has not hardened into pain, more a hint than a hurt.

entries.definition: uncomfortable because of possible danger or trouble
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Locates the discomfort in looming danger or trouble rather than in the flesh, and its mildness is exactly what makes it sound like a warning.
examples: made things warm for the bookies

entries.definition: characterized by physical misery
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A degree past *miserable* on the same misery — abject, with no dignity left to the body it describes.
examples: spent a wretched night on the floor

entries.definition: requiring more than usually expected or thought due; especially great patience and effort and skill
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Plain and unheated - it names the size of what is asked without ruling on whether asking it is fair, where *hard-to-please* has already convicted someone.
examples: a baby can be so demanding

entries.definition: requiring precise accuracy
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the weight on the standard itself, so the precision reads as a measure to be met rather than a temper to be humoured.

entries.definition: requiring precise accuracy
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The formal, cool-surfaced twin of *exacting* - the same insistence on precision, pitched at a distance.
examples: became more exigent over his pronunciation

entries.definition: (of persons) fussy and demanding
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Disparaging - the fussiness makes the demand a flaw in the person, which *exacting* never does.
examples: his father was a hard-to-please taskmaster

entries.definition: (of persons) fussy and demanding
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The open spelling carries the same verdict but reads as a running remark about someone rather than a label fixed to them.

entries.definition: demanding or needing attention, affection, or reassurance to an excessive degree
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Belittling and intimate - the excess is emotional appetite, and the word tips toward pity where *hard-to-please* stays at irritation.

entries.definition: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving - the strictness registers as discipline worth having, where *tight* only pinches.

entries.definition: severe and unremitting in making demands
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds a forbidding manner to the severity - the unrelenting demand arrives with a chill that *strict* does not carry.

entries.definition: severe and unremitting in making demands
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat word for the same unrelenting severity, stating it without colouring it as harshness.

entries.definition: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Cool and administrative, stating how tightly the rules bind without either praising or resenting the binding.

entries.definition: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The informal one, and the constriction is felt - the rules squeeze rather than uphold anything.

entries.definition: much wanted
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Loads the wanting with hunger, so the thing is not merely worth having but longed for hard, far greedier than the flat *in demand*.

entries.definition: capable of arousing sexual desire
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Relishing rather than clinical, it savours the desire the thing arouses where *sexually attractive* merely reports it.

entries.definition: worth having or seeking or achieving
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The measured, unheated verdict — it says a thing is worth having without claiming anyone is straining after it, which is what *coveted* adds.

entries.definition: causing envy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises a thing by pointing at the sourness it stirs in whoever lacks it, so the approval arrives through someone else's discontent.

entries.definition: much wanted
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: States much-wantedness as a plain fact about a thing's standing, with none of the appetite audible in *coveted*.

entries.definition: very desirable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and relishing, it heaps the desirability higher than the sober *desirable* and sounds pleased with itself for saying so.

entries.definition: more desirable than another
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A comparative and nothing more — it rates one thing above another without claiming either is wanted much at all.

entries.definition: more desirable than another
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Settles the comparison that *preferable* is still arguing, presenting the ranking as already decided rather than urged.

entries.definition: capable of arousing sexual desire
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Flat and explicit, naming the arousal outright without a trace of the relish in *delectable*.

entries.definition: much wanted
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The hyphen compresses that same pursuit into a single modifier that can sit in front of the noun it flatters.

entries.definition: much wanted
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the wanting into motion — the thing is actively pursued, where *in demand* leaves it a standing condition.

entries.definition: requiring full use of your abilities or resources
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving - it treats the full call on your abilities and resources as a reach worth making rather than a weight to be borne.

entries.definition: difficult to accomplish; demanding considerable mental effort and skill
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and weighty - it dwells on the sustained mental effort and skill the thing exacts before it will be accomplished, heavier in the mouth than *hard*.
examples: the arduous work of preparing a dictionary

entries.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mildly disapproving - the difficulty sits in the handling, since any move you make risks the pain or embarrassment the thing carries.
examples: awkward (or embarrassing or difficult) moments in the discussion
an awkward pause followed his remark

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the great mental demand where understanding fails - the thing does not merely resist solution, it leaves you at a loss.

entries.definition: having concealed difficulty
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Warns of a snare - the difficulty is concealed until you are into it, so the word marks the thing as harder than it lets on.

entries.definition: requiring full use of your abilities or resources
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns that same full call on everything you have into an invitation to rise to it, so the demand reads as a spur where *problematic* reads as a fault.
examples: performed the most challenging task without a mistake

entries.definition: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and unemotive - it registers that effort is required to do, grasp or bear the thing, without hinting whether that effort is worth spending, as *challenging* does.
examples: nesting places on the cliffs are difficult of access

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The difficulty is in the slipping away: comprehension seems within reach and will not close on it, unlike the frank obstruction of *knotty*.

entries.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the discomfort squarely on the face of whoever has to deal with it, naming the exposure that *awkward* leaves implied.
examples: awkward (or embarrassing or difficult) moments in the discussion

entries.definition: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The blunt, plain-spoken version of *difficult* for the same demand, taking effort of body, mind or endurance as it comes and softening none of it.
examples: why is it so hard for you to keep a secret?

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Gives the mental demand a shape - a tangle to be picked apart strand by strand, rather than the blank wall of *baffling*.
examples: I faced the knotty problem of what to have for breakfast

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Labels the demanding thing a problem outright, a mild verdict against it where *tough* only reports the demand.

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Stiffer and more formal than *problematic* for the same verdict, its extra syllable adding weight rather than force.

entries.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal - it makes the trouble something you are caught in and cannot step cleanly out of, lighter in tone than *unenviable* and no easier to escape.

entries.definition: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and almost respectful of the difficulty - it sizes up the mental demand as something to be taken on and says nothing against it.

entries.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: An understated verdict that condemns by observation - the thing is framed as unwished-for, and the word damns it without raising its voice.
examples: in the unenviable position of resorting to an act he had planned to save for the climax of the campaign

entries.definition: nonexistent
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and faintly formal, stating the nonexistence with none of the note of shortfall in *lacking*.

entries.definition: completely wanting or lacking
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Bleak - the total lack is a desolate condition rather than the cool fact *devoid* states.
